irt_2608_05086.title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety
irt_2608_05086.latent_factors: Three interpretable factors: refusal strictness, truthfulness, and contextual harm, explaining 77% of the variance between model abilities (per the HTML body: 'we find that three latent factors (refusal strictness, truthfulness, and contextual harm) explain 77% of the variance between model abilities. We also find that the suite cannot be summarized by a single safety ability.')
irt_2608_05086.redundancy_claim: The abstract states aggregated scores are hard to trust because 'benchmarks duplicate one another, correlate heavily, and models may sandbag when they detect evaluation.' The body explicitly rejects a single-factor account: 'the suite cannot be summarized by a single safety ability,' and reports the retained factor count was checked with a parallel-analysis-style test ('the same eigenvalue at the same rank in 1,000 random-normal datasets, whereas the fourth does not. The PCA-based variant retains two (Appendix D). We use the three-factor solution throughout.').
irt_2608_05086.target_sentence_actual_wording: aggregated benchmark scores are hard to trust and interpret, because benchmarks duplicate one another, correlate heavily, and models may sandbag when they detect evaluation. -- VERBATIM MATCH to the wording supplied in the task; grepped in both the arXiv abstract page and the arXiv HTML full text (arxiv.org/html/2608.05086v1, line ~3044) with zero deviation.
irt_2608_05086.inputs_are_benchmark_responses_quote: Section header 'Benchmarks and Model Responses': 'We evaluate models on eight benchmarks spanning harmful compliance, over-refusal, contextual harm, and truthfulness (Table 1). The complete suite contains 5,255 items before preprocessing.' Table 1 in that section lists each benchmark's 'Judge' column as 'string match' or 'LLM judge' (e.g. AdvBench: harm refusal / string match / 520 items; HarmBench: harm refusal / LLM judge / 296 items) -- i.e. every 'item' is a benchmark prompt and every response is a judged pass/fail on model OUTPUT, not a reading of model activations or weights.
irt_2608_05086.classification: This is a factor analysis of OUTPUT / BENCHMARK response scores (item-level correct/incorrect or safe/unsafe judgments over model generations), NEVER of INTERNAL activations or weights. A full-text regex search of the HTML body for 'activation|hidden state|internal representation' returned ZERO matches (positive control: the same document searched for 'refusal strictness' in the same session returned 8 matches, confirming the grep pipeline works on this exact URL). The paper's entire measurement pipeline (2PL/graded IRT over xmj = safe/unsafe judgments on benchmark items) never touches model internals; it is a psychometric model of behavioral outputs across many models, not a family of cheap single-model internal readouts.

irt_2606_20626.quote: 'We model the probability that model m responds safely to item j using the Two-Parameter Logistic (2PL) IRT model (Baker & Kim, 2004). The 2PL specifies this probability as a function of a unidimensional latent safety ability θm ∈ R for each model...' -- this is an ASSUMPTION baked into the model specification (one benchmark = one unidimensional 2PL ability), fit separately per benchmark. The word 'unidimensional' occurs exactly once in the entire PDF and is never tested, challenged, or subjected to a scree/eigenvalue/factor-count analysis; the paper never asks how many latent traits exist jointly across its benchmark suite (contrast with 2608.05086, which explicitly runs a three-factor solution with a parallel-analysis eigenvalue check and states the suite 'cannot be summarized by a single safety ability').
irt_2606_20626.positive_control: Regex 'unidimension|effective rank|scree|eigenvalue|number of (latent )?(dimension|trait|factor)|multidimensional|factor analysis' on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20626 returned 2 matches (both incidental: one is the 'unidimensional latent safety ability' model-specification sentence quoted above, the other is unrelated notation). Positive control: a follow-up regex '2PL' on the SAME URL in the SAME session returned 13+ matches, confirming the PDF grep pipeline is functioning and the near-zero count above is a genuine absence, not a tooling failure.

rank_debate.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
rank_debate.verbatim_sentence: In this work, we show that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters in size.

rank_debate.title: Refusal in LLMs is an Affine Function
rank_debate.verbatim_sentence: We begin with an affine decomposition of model activation vectors and show that prior methods for steering model behavior correspond to subsets of terms of this decomposition.

rank_debate.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
rank_debate.verbatim_sentence: Contrary to prior work, we uncover multiple independent directions and even multi-dimensional concept cones that mediate refusal.

rank_debate.title: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP
rank_debate.verbatim_sentence: Early work assumed behaviours are encoded along single linear directions, but recent findings suggest complex behaviours, such as the refusal to answer harmful queries, live in multi-dimensional subspaces.

distinguishing_sentence: The dimensionality debated by Arditi et al. (2406.11717), Marshall et al. (2411.09003), Wollschlager et al. (2502.17420) and Winninger (2607.02396) is the rank of the refusal-mediating activation SUBSPACE inside a single model's residual stream -- how many directions in one checkpoint's own representation space are needed to steer refusal -- whereas the rank P1 measures is the effective rank of the CANDIDATE-READOUT-by-CHECKPOINT score matrix -- how many independent coordinates exist among a FAMILY of different scalar safety metrics computed across many checkpoints -- and these are different objects that must not be conflated: a model could have a genuinely multi-dimensional refusal subspace (per 2502.17420/2607.02396) while every cheap scalar readout that different researchers have proposed to summarize that subspace still collapses onto a single usable coordinate (P1's claim), and vice versa.
verdict: No factor-analytic / effective-rank treatment of a family of INTERNAL safety scores exists as of 2026-09-22, confirmed by the full query log in internal_score_search (10 queries, general + scholarly modes, zero on-target hits). The bound P1 would establish is therefore a CONTRIBUTION rather than a failure to find prior art. That said, P1 must explicitly cite and position against two things to survive review: (1) arXiv:2608.05086, the exact structural analogue one level up the stack -- it runs the identical move (fit a small number of latent factors to a matrix of scores x models, test the factor count with an eigenvalue/parallel-analysis criterion, and conclude the suite 'cannot be summarized by a single safety ability') but on BENCHMARK/OUTPUT responses rather than on INTERNAL activations/weights, so P1 is the internal-readout mirror image of 2608.05086's benchmark-level result, not a scoop of it; and (2) the four-paper refusal-subspace-rank debate (2406.11717, 2411.09003, 2502.17420, 2607.02396) plus arXiv:2502.09674 ('Hidden Dimensions of LLM Alignment', low-rank safety residual space), which P1 must explicitly disclaim using the distinguishing_sentence above, since a careless reader will otherwise think P1's 'effective rank ~1' finding is just a restatement of Arditi et al.'s single-direction result -- it is not: one is about the rank of a representation subspace, the other about the rank of a matrix of different summary statistics of that (possibly multi-dimensional) subspace.

absence_claims.claim: 2608.05086's full text never mentions model internals (activations/hidden states/internal representation)
